articles.title: May 22 is Astronomy Day — Welcome visitors to the San Jose Astronomical Association program at The Tech Museum. Join us at any SJAA activities below. See page 5 for star party information.
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting an Astronomy Day program at The Tech Museum on May 22, inviting visitors to participate in their activities. Attendees are encouraged to join SJAA events, with further details on star party information available on page 5.

articles.title: SJAA Activities Calendar
articles.summary: The SJAA Activities Calendar outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's events for May, June, and July, featuring general meetings with guest speakers, multiple star parties at various locations like Houge Park and Fremont Peak, and specialized observational astronomy classes. It also lists a special weekend event at Glacier Point in Yosemite National Park and opportunities for future speakers.

articles.title: The Celestial Tourist Speaks
articles.summary: Jay Reynolds Freeman details his prolonged anticipation and eventual acquisition of a used Astro-Physics 6-inch f/8 triplet refractor in late 1998, with "first light" delayed until April due to an uncommonly bad California winter. The article describes the unique process of purchasing the high-end instrument from a friend, including an unusual pricing negotiation, and mentions his current difficulty selling his old Meade 127 ED. He also provides a brief description of the new telescope and its accompanying, somewhat eccentric, accessories.

articles.title: The Celestial Tourist Speaks
articles.summary: The author recounts their "first light" experience with a new 6-inch refractor at a public star party, detailing the logistical challenges of transport and setup. Despite initial hurdles, the author was highly impressed with the telescope's optical performance, especially its excellent color correction and clear views of the Moon, Mars, and winter galactic clusters. The new refractor received positive feedback from the public and other observers, affirming the author's satisfaction with the new acquisition.

articles.title: How To Write Your Own "Mooning" Column
articles.summary: The author, David North, explains his decision to purchase an Astro-Physics 6-inch f/8 refractor, despite owning a larger Celestron 14 and often advocating for aperture supremacy. His reasons include a personal enjoyment of owning various high-quality telescopes, a desire to further investigate the relative performance between high-end refractors and larger instruments, and potential future uses for public star parties.

articles.title: Meteor Watch
articles.summary: This 'Meteor Watch' article for June 1999 advises readers on observing the June Bootids meteor shower, suggesting a watch on June 27, especially from the U.S. East Coast, despite a full moon. It also offers lunar observation tips, highlighting specific dates for optimal viewing of the Moon's limbs due to libration. Additionally, the article points out an excellent opportunity on June 14 to spot a young moon shortly after sunset due to its high northern declination.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article, 'The Shallow Sky' by Akkana Peck, offers astronomical observing tips for June, particularly highlighting 'The Gang Of Four,' a self-named group of prominent lunar craters (Langrenus, Vendelinus, Petavius, Furnerius) visible on the early waxing moon, and encourages observers to compare their diverse features. It also provides guidance for observing Mars in the early evening, detailing visible surface features, and Venus, noting its visibility and conjunctions with the Beehive cluster and a crescent moon. The author emphasizes accessible observation for amateur astronomers.

articles.title: Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article provides an observational guide for various planets visible in the shallow sky, including Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. It offers practical advice such as using filters for bright objects like Venus and finder charts for fainter ones, while detailing their visibility, brightness, and positions throughout the month. The author encourages observers to share their sightings and experiences.

articles.title: What to Expect at an SJAA Star Party
articles.summary: This article provides guidance on what to expect at San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) star parties, aimed at new or curious individuals. It highlights the informal nature of these gatherings, the diverse range of telescopes and expert observers, and encourages attendees to bring their own equipment or simply enjoy shared views under the night sky. The article specifically details the popular Fremont Peak location as a prime spot for dark-sky observing and public viewing sessions.

articles.title: About Star Parties
articles.summary: The article describes two distinct SJAA star party locations—Henry Coe State Park for dark-sky observing and Houge Park for public outreach and social gatherings with moon views. It also includes a detailed personal observing report from April 1999 in Australia, chronicling the successful sighting of Comet Hale-Bopp near the Large Magellanic Cloud.

articles.title: Comet Comments
articles.summary: The article reports on several recent comet discoveries by both professional programs and amateur astronomers, including C/1999 H1 (Lee) found at an Australian star party. It details the visibility, expected brightness, and orbital characteristics of these new comets, such as those found by SOHO, LINEAR, and Catalina programs. The piece also highlights the rare instances of successful amateur comet discoveries made at star parties, drawing parallels with past finds by individuals like Don Machholz and Thomas Bopp.

articles.title: Ephemerides
articles.summary: This document provides detailed ephemerides for two comets, C/1999 H1 (Lee) and C/1998 T1 (LINEAR). For each comet, tabular data is presented, listing dates from May to July along with their respective Right Ascension, Declination, Elevation, and predicted Sky Magnitude. This information is vital for astronomers and observers to accurately locate and track these celestial objects.

articles.title: Elements
articles.summary: This document details the orbital elements for two celestial objects, "Lee" and "LINEAR (T1)", providing key astronomical parameters such as perihelion dates, distances, eccentricity, inclination, and orbital periods. The data includes references to Minor Planet Circulars (MPC) for both objects. Additionally, the document contains contact information for Don Machholz and a personal request from Jim Van Nuland regarding a lent item.

articles.title: Loan Program Supporters
articles.summary: The article expresses gratitude to Akkana Pack, Alexander Koczur, and Manoj Khambete for their contributions to a loaner program. Donations included two eyepieces, a storage container for an astrophotography scope, and a monetary contribution, all supporting the program.

articles.title: IC 2220 — The Toby Jug Nebula
articles.summary: Prompted by a young boy, the author recounts their discovery and observation of IC 2220, the Toby Jug Nebula, during an astrotourism trip to Ayers Rock. They describe the challenge of visually locating this faint reflection nebula, which surrounds the bright star HD 65750, noting it is more impressive photographically. The article highlights the shared excitement of the group, culminating in the young boy successfully finding the nebula himself through a telescope.

articles.title: Lunar Phases:
articles.summary: The document presents a concise table detailing the dates and times for significant lunar phases, including Last Quarter, New Moon, First Quarter, and Full Moon. For each phase, it provides the exact date and time, alongside its corresponding rise, transit, and set times.

articles.title: Nearer Planets:
articles.summary: This document provides an astronomical ephemeris for the 'Nearer Planets' – Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn – for three specific dates (7th, 17th, and 27th) of an unspecified month. For each planet and date, it details their rise, transit, and set times, along with their right ascension, declination, distance in Astronomical Units (A.U.), and apparent magnitude (Mag.). This data serves as a guide for observers tracking planetary positions and visibility in the night sky.

articles.title: SOL Star Type G2V
articles.summary: This article classifies "SOL" as a G2V type star and presents a table of astronomical data, including its rise, transit, and set times, along with Right Ascension and Declination for several dates in June. It also poses a general question regarding the presence of intelligent life within the system.

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight:
articles.summary: This document, titled 'Astronomical Twilight,' presents a concise table detailing the beginning and end times of astronomical twilight for several specific Julian Dates. It serves as a direct reference for the daily duration of this celestial phenomenon.

articles.title: Sidereal Time:
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical data for June 1999, specifically detailing Sidereal Time (Transit Right Ascension at Local Midnight) for various dates. It also highlights the 'DARKEST SAT. NIGHT' on June 12, 1999, listing key times such as sunset, twilight end, moonset, and dawn begin, along with the total hours of darkness.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a loaner scope program, making telescopes available to any SJAA member. Members interested in borrowing a scope should contact Mike Koop via email or phone, leaving a message if necessary.

articles.title: Stored Scopes
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers "Stored Scopes" for immediate loan, which are telescopes kept at various members' homes. Members interested in borrowing one of these scopes, including various Newtonians, a Dobson, and a Refractor, should contact Mike Koop to arrange a pickup at any SJAA event.

articles.title: Current Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes currently on loan, indicating their description, borrower, and due date. Individuals interested in borrowing a scope will be added to a waiting list until it becomes available. The list includes various Dobsonians, a Solar Scope, and a C8 for astrophotography.

articles.title: Extended Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists astronomical telescopes that have had their loan periods extended, offering them for potential new borrowers. It details various scopes, their current custodians, and due dates, while also requesting assistance in contacting a specific borrower and inquiring about storage space for equipment.

articles.title: Waiting List:
articles.summary: This document is a waiting list detailing items currently borrowed or reserved. It shows one entry: a 'Solar Scope' currently associated with 'Bill Maney' as the borrower.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the officers and board of directors for an organization, detailing each person's position, name, and contact phone number. It includes a President, Vice President, Secretary, and six Directors, noting that the Treasurer position is currently vacant.

articles.title: Ephemeris Staff
articles.summary: The document provides a staff directory for "Ephemeris," listing individuals and companies responsible for key roles such as editing, circulation, and printing. Each entry includes a name and a contact phone number for easy reference.

articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: This document encourages members to submit their articles for publication in the SJAA Ephemeris. Submissions should be sent directly to the editors via the provided email address, ephemeris@whiteoaks.com.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: This document is a periodical publication statement for the 'SJAA Ephemeris,' the monthly newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), published 12 times a year. It provides the association's mailing address and instructions for subscribing to or unsubscribing from the SJAA Mailing List.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing fees for new or renewal memberships ($15 for regular, $6 for junior) and an optional Sky & Telescope magazine subscription add-on ($27). It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment via mail or at an SJAA meeting, along with the association's contact information and mailing address.
